## Problem / Motivation

CubeMaster scheduling filters (`cpu`, `mem`) rely on per-node **allocated quota** fields (`QuotaCpuUsage`, `QuotaMemUsage`) loaded from **Redis** into `localcache` (see `loopUpdateMetric` → `getNodeMetricFromRedis` → `updateNodeMetric`).

Cubelet already computes the correct values by summing running sandboxes' `ResourceWithOverHead` and exposes them via:

- `GET http://<cubelet>:9998/v1/metrics/scheduler`
- fields: `quota_cpu_usage` (milli), `quota_mem_mb_usage` (MB), `mvm_num`, etc.
  (`Cubelet/services/cubebox/metric.go`, `plugins/cube/internals/metric/handler.go`)

However, in the **open-source tree**, nothing in the production path pulls Cubelet metrics and writes them to Redis:

- **Cubelet** does not write Redis.
- **CubeMaster** only **reads** Redis for node metrics; it does not update `quota_*_usage` on sandbox create/destroy.
- The only writers of `quota_cpu_usage` / `quota_mem_mb_usage` in this repo are:
  - `CubeMaster/integration/mock_init.go` (integration tests)
  - `deploy/one-click/scripts/one-click/seed-cubemaster-metrics.sh` (static/demo values, not live Cubelet data)

As a result, a self-contained OSS deployment (without the seed script) tends to keep `quota_*_usage` at 0 in Redis. The scheduler then behaves as if nodes have no allocated quota, weakening `cpufilter` / `memfilter` and making quota-based capacity control unreliable—especially with default host quota oversubscription (`5/4` memory).

This gap also affects operators who want cluster autoscaling or inventory signals aligned with scheduling (same Redis fields / `/internal/node`).

## Proposed Solution

Please provide an **official, supported** way to close the loop:

**Option A (recommended): small sidecar / daemon in `deploy/`**

- Periodically discover nodes (e.g. `GET /internal/meta/nodes`).
- Scrape `GET /v1/metrics/scheduler` on each healthy Cubelet.
- `HSET` Redis hash keyed by `ins_id` with the same schema as `localcache.RedisNodeInfo`:
  - `ins_id`, `quota_cpu_usage`, `quota_mem_mb_usage`, `mvm_num`, `realtime_create_num`, `update_at` (RFC3339 UTC).
- Document as a **required** component for multi-node / production (alongside MySQL and Redis).
- Wire into `one-click` / `install-compute` instead of (or in addition to) static `seed-cubemaster-metrics.sh`.

**Option B: Master updates Redis on create/destroy**

- Increment/decrement `quota_*_usage` in Redis when sandbox create/destroy succeeds on a node.
- Requires reconciliation with Cubelet truth (restarts, failed destroys, manual cleanup).

**Option C: Cubelet pushes metrics to Redis**

- Cubelet writes the same hash fields directly (config: Redis addr/password).

Any option is fine; the important part is a **documented, maintained** production path so scheduling and observability use **live** quota occupancy.

## Alternatives Considered

- Relying on `seed-cubemaster-metrics.sh`: only suitable for demo; values are not tied to real sandbox load.
- External/private “ReportGW”: may exist in some deployments but is not in this repository; OSS users have no supported integration.
- Reading Cubelet only from a custom autoscaler: does not fix CubeMaster scheduling unless Redis is still updated for Master.

## Additional Context

**Data flow today (OSS):**

```text
Cubelet  --HTTP /v1/metrics/scheduler-->  (no writer in repo)
                                              |
integration mock / seed script --HSET-->  Redis  --HGETALL-->  CubeMaster localcache --> scheduler
```
Relevant code:

- Read path: `CubeMaster/pkg/localcache/redis_cache.go`, `node_cache.go` (updateNodeMetric)
- Filters: `CubeMaster/pkg/selector/filter/cpufilter.go`, memfilter.go
- Metric source: `Cubelet/services/cubebox/metric.go`

Suggested acceptance criteria:

- After creating sandboxes on a node, Redis `quota_cpu_usage` / `quota_mem_mb_usage` increase without running integration tests or manual seed scripts.
- After destroying all sandboxes, usage returns to ~0.
- GET /internal/node reflects the same values as Redis (within `sync_metric_data_interval`).
- Multi-node deploy guide lists the metric sync component as required.
